B05-L01 - Cloud data mental model: storage, compute, network
Cloud diagrams feel like a list of product names until you separate four questions: where data lives, what work runs on it, how systems
can reach each other, and who/what is allowed to act. Engineers make those boundaries explicit before selecting services.
Classify a data requirement into storage, compute, network/connection and identity; explain why a service name alone is not an
Course 1 report refresh, sharing and basic cloud awareness. You do not need Azure/Fabric administration.
Picture a warehouse building. Storage is the shelves, compute is the workers/machines, network is the roads and locked doors, identity is the badge
that says who may enter and what they may do.
the processing resources that read/transform/query data
the path and restrictions between systems
a human, group or application identity used to authorize actions
a non-human application identity used for automated access
Use Microsoft Fabric overview as current reference. Optional visual: John Savill 02:49-09:44. After watching, close it and draw four
boxes: storage / compute / network / identity; place one Distribution source decision in each.
What you already know as an analyst: a report has a source, refresh and access.
What changes in engineering: each dependency becomes an explicit architecture boundary.
Why engineers care: failures and security problems often happen at a different boundary from the visible report.
Small worked example: WMS_SQL is on-prem storage; a cloud engine may compute over landed data; a secure private connection crosses the
network boundary; SPN-PIPE can be the scheduled identity.
Real engineering version: C3-07 will provision and operate concrete platform resources. Here you learn the decision grammar first.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B05 Cloud Platform Essentials | INTERNAL QA RC1
Open B05_CLOUD_PLATFORM_PRACTICE_RC1.xlsx -> Source_Inventory and L01_Cloud_Mental_Model. Classify WMS_SQL,
Carrier_API, Vendor_Files and Semantic_Model across the four dimensions.
You should see that one source can create several different requirements. “Use Fabric” is not yet an answer because it does not state
data placement, processing, connection path or identity.
The method works because requirements constrain architecture. A private SQL source creates a connection problem even if the
destination service is healthy; a scheduled pipeline creates an identity problem even if a human can access the workspace.
• Choosing a product before writing the requirement.
• Treating storage and compute as the same thing.
• Assuming every source needs a gateway.
• Using a person’s login as an automation identity without discussing ownership.
Take one source only. Ask four literal questions: Where does its data live? What must process it? Can the destination reach it? Who/what should
Fresh case: an e-commerce company has a cloud API, a private finance database and a daily file drop. Write one storage, compute,
network and identity concern for each.
Every decision points to a stated source/freshness/security requirement. Cloud sources are not automatically labeled “gateway”;
private sources are not magically reachable.
Without notes, explain the four-box model in 60-90 seconds and give one failure example for each box.
Save your first attempt before review. After review, change WMS freshness from 60 minutes to 10 minutes and decide which
boundaries might need a different design.
Save four-box sketch + source classification + one failure chain + changed retry + confidence 1-5. Ready only when you can classify a fresh case

B05-L02 - Fabric, OneLake, lakehouse and warehouse as one
You need one real platform to make cloud ideas concrete, but memorizing Fabric screens would waste Bridge time. The useful skill is
mapping platform pieces to requirements and knowing when storage, item type and consumer experience differ.
Explain tenant/workspace/item/OneLake at a beginner level; compare lakehouse and warehouse fit; reason about copy versus
reference/shortcut without requiring a live tenant.
B05-L01 four-box model plus Course 1 Power BI workspace familiarity.
Think of one campus (tenant), several secured rooms (workspaces), tools/objects inside each room (items), and a common organization-wide
storage foundation underneath (OneLake). A lakehouse and warehouse are different working shapes over data, not moral “better/worse” choices.
a Fabric object such as lakehouse or warehouse
data-lake storage with table/query capabilities for engineering/analytics
relational analytical store optimized for SQL-centric warehouse work
access data in place rather than copying it when supported and appropriate

1:00:43-1:13:12. After watching, write one lakehouse-fit case, one warehouse-fit case and one case where avoiding a second copy
What you already know as an analyst: workspaces and semantic models organize reporting work.
What changes in engineering: you reason about shared storage, multiple data workloads and how data is exposed without unnecessary copies.
Why engineers care: duplication, ownership and workload choice affect reliability, cost and governance.
Small worked example: retain large raw files in shared storage; use a lakehouse-style path for file/table engineering and a warehouse when
SQL-relational serving is the dominant need; do not copy a huge archive merely because another engine needs access if a governed reference is

warehouse / reference-copy pattern and write the rejected alternative.
You should see decisions tied to workload and data behavior, not “lakehouse is modern so choose lakehouse.” OneLake does not
mean every user can read every item/data set.
Separating organization/workspace/item from the storage foundation prevents a common beginner error: confusing shared storage
architecture with unrestricted access or one universal compute engine.
• Treating Fabric as the definition of cloud data engineering.
• Saying OneLake means one physical copy in every case or universal read permission.
• Choosing lakehouse/warehouse by popularity instead of workload.
• Copying large data with no reason or ownership plan.
Return to two questions: What shape/use must the consumer have? Does the data need to be copied, or can an authorized engine reference it

Explain tenant, workspace, item and OneLake to a non-technical manager without using circular definitions.
After saving attempt and using review, change the large archive requirement from “monthly analysis” to “multiple engines need daily
access.” Re-evaluate copy/reference and serving choice.

Human/group/service identities have different responsibilities. Cloud APIs do not receive an on-prem gateway just because gateways

Least privilege reduces blast radius while explicit connection boundaries make failures diagnosable. The network can fail
independently from identity, and identity can fail independently from the data itself.

• Confusing workspace role with row/data authorization.

B05-L04 - Freshness, monitoring and failure ownership
A green run is not the same as fresh, complete or trustworthy data. Engineers need evidence that data met the business freshness
promise and a named response when it did not.
Turn a business freshness need into SLA/trigger/tolerance/owner/validation; diagnose stale-data incidents and require post-recovery
B05-L01-L03 and Course 1 refresh validation. No orchestration platform is required.
Imagine a train board. “Train engine running” does not prove the passenger arrived on time. You need scheduled arrival, actual arrival, delay
tolerance, owner and a rule for informing waiting passengers.
agreed maximum age/arrival target for usable data
whether a job execution reported success/failure
how current the accepted data actually is
evidence used to detect a condition
checks proving recovered output is complete/correct/fresh
Use current Fabric monitoring hub for run/history/error concepts and Microsoft on-premises gateway overview for private-source
dependency. After reading, write one signal -> owner -> recovery -> validation -> consumer message chain for each Distribution
What you already know as an analyst: refresh and control totals tell you whether a report is current/trustworthy.
What changes in engineering: freshness becomes an operational contract with monitoring, owner, recovery and downstream communication.
Why engineers care: a pipeline may be green while source data is late, partial or stale.
Small worked example: Carrier_API target 30 min; if OAuth expires, signal is 401, owner repairs credential path, rerun is not enough -
count/window/freshness must be revalidated, then consumers get status.
Real engineering version: C3-03/C3-08 implement orchestration/observability. B05 teaches the acceptance logic first.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B05 Cloud Platform Essentials | INTERNAL QA RC1

You should see separate technical and data states. A successful rerun still requires source-to-output completeness and freshness
Operational contracts make “is it ready?” answerable. Without a target and validation signal, monitoring becomes decorative; without
an owner, a detected failure can remain unresolved.
• Rerunning until green with no reconciliation.
• No owner for late external files.
• Promising “real time” without a measurable threshold.
Write the sentence: “Consumers may use this output when ___.” Fill it with freshness, completeness and quality evidence. Then ask who acts when

Think of a relay race. The analyst does not throw a vague idea over the wall; the baton has labels: what data, for which decision, when it must arrive,
who may use it, what proves correctness and what happens on failure.
objective condition that determines whether delivery is acceptable
checking what downstream work may change when an upstream source/definition changes

Lesson

Failure-first recall
- A cloud-accessible SaaS/API/object store does not automatically need an on-premises gateway. A
private/on-prem source does need an explicit secure connection boundary.

belong in learner workbooks.

downstream validation and consumer communication.
- Architecture choices must name a rejected alternative and the requirement that makes it worse.

needs.

consumer freshness communication.

C2B / B05 / ASTRA PARITY RC4
B05 Gate A Protected Review - Manufacturing Quality
Cloud architecture evidence, operations and changed retry
C2B / B05 / CHECKPOINT45
Page 1
Protected review - saved genuine Gate attempt required
Open only after the matching Gate attempt is saved. Diagnose, repair, close the review and produce
changed evidence. Later Gates remain explicitly assigned fresh reassessments.
Non-negotiable case evidence
- Private MES and historian require an explicit secure private/on-prem connection boundary; QMS API,
Azure Blob and cloud/private ERP replica must be evaluated separately.
- Freshness differs by source: historian 5 min, MES 15 min, QMS 30 min, image metadata hourly, ERP
cost daily, certified model hourly. Architecture must not flatten these into one schedule.
- GRP-QA needs curated quality analysis, not raw secrets/admin. Plant managers are read-only
consumers. SPN-MFG is a nonhuman least-privilege pipeline identity. Vendor access is exceptional, not
default workspace membership.
- Inspection images are large unstructured evidence; duplication must be justified.
- Incidents: firewall/gateway break, token expiry, accidental Contributor grant. Each requires signal, owner,
recovery, post-validation and communication.

C2B / B05 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT45
Page 2
Architecture and operations rubric
- Start from location, format, sensitivity, freshness, failure tolerance and consumer need before naming
Fabric items/services.
- Separate storage from compute and choose copy/reference/shortcut only with a workload reason.
- Distinguish private/on-prem connectivity from ordinary cloud access; name the network/gateway owner
where applicable.
- Separate workspace/item control-plane permissions from data-plane access. Use human groups and
nonhuman identities deliberately.
- For every freshness SLA, define schedule/trigger, tolerance, monitoring signal, owner, recovery/backfill
and post-recovery validation.
- For security/schema incidents, state block/quarantine/partial-publish behavior and lineage/consumer
impact.
- Include a rejected alternative and objective acceptance tests in the handoff.
Critical failures
- Ungrounded service selection or “Fabric does everything” reasoning.
- Gateway invented for cloud sources or omitted for a private source.
- Broad Contributor/Admin used as a data-access shortcut.
- One refresh schedule used despite different SLAs.
- Incident has no owner, recovery, post-validation or stale-data communication.
- External user receives confidential detail or broad workspace access without justification.
- Hidden live-tenant dependency required to pass a reasoning assessment.

C2B / B05 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT45
Page 3
Repair and changed retry route
- Keep the original attempt append-only.
- Open only this matching review after the saved genuine attempt.
- Repair the smallest weak competency using targeted remediation.
- Close the review and solve a changed micro-scenario with different source/network/security/freshness
facts.
- Save the changed evidence. Gate B/C still require the existing explicit fresh full-retest assignment.
Next route
PASS -> B06. Otherwise repair; Gate B remains sealed.
